subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction fails with 'Thread group size (1024) exceeds maximum threads per threadgroup (896)'

question: Should failed overflow compaction for local/OpenAI-compatible providers remain fail-closed, persist/recover through the broader overflow give_up marker path, or add a backend-specific request tuning surface?
rationale: Changing the give_up branch affects replay safety, session continuity, provider behavior, and whether OpenClaw should add new config surface for a backend-specific failure whose request contract is not yet proven.

options.title: Provider-agnostic recovery first
options.body: Design a safe degraded recovery or durable marker path for compaction-provider errors before adding any MLX-specific thread setting.

options.title: Keep fail-closed semantics
options.body: Leave the blocked reset/new outcome as the safe default and improve diagnostics or docs around switching compaction models and provider params.

options.title: Add MLX-specific tuning
options.body: Introduce a dedicated compaction/provider parameter only after maintainers confirm MLX exposes a stable field that existing extra_body cannot cover.

recommendation.title: Provider-agnostic recovery first
recommendation.body: Design a safe degraded recovery or durable marker path for compaction-provider errors before adding any MLX-specific thread setting.

likelyOwner.reason: The current overflow give_up branch and shipped release path are tied to Vincent Koc in blame and -S history.
